title: Tiered safeguard orchestrator for Optimize auto-deploys
creator: Priya Khatri
description:
Problem: Optimize suggests batching and KV-caching profiles that can materially change latency and tail behavior. We need a safe, automated way to apply high-confidence suggestions while preventing regressions and providing fast rollback.

Goal: Implement a Tiered Safeguard Orchestrator (TSO) that can: 1) evaluate suggestions by simulated workload and observed field telemetry, 2) gate auto-application through configurable policy tiers (staging, canary, graduated), 3) require human approvals for higher-risk changes, and 4) provide deterministic rollback and forensic audit logs. The system should be compatible with Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and integrate with Rollouts, Console dashboards, and Optimize's suggestion engine.
acceptance_criteria: TSO can ingest a suggestion payload and produce a deterministic risk score and recommended tier (staging/canary/auto).
Configurable policy matrix exists that maps risk, customer SLA, and model-class to required approvals and rollout velocity.
Automated canary deployment path deploys to a configurable traffic slice, collects metrics for a defined observation window, and either graduates or reverts based on thresholds.
Full audit trail is emitted to the platform audit log (immutable event per state transition) and surfaces in Console's Rollout trace for operators.
Rollback completes within the configured SLA (default 2 minutes) and KV cache is invalidated atomically where applicable.
End-to-end tests run in CI that simulate a regressing suggestion and validate that TSO prevents promotion without manual signoff.
design_summary: Introduce a middle-layer service (tso-service) that sits between Optimize suggestion generator and the existing rollout enactor. TSO will: 1) call a simulation runner in a seeded synthetic environment to estimate percentiles and cost delta, 2) compute a graded confidence score using telemetry + simulation + historical suggestion outcomes, 3) consult a policy lattice to decide gating (auto, canary, manual), 4) trigger rollout via existing rollout-controller with canary parameters when allowed, and 5) orchestrate rollback and postmortem artifacts on failure. Policy rules are declarative YAML stored in config service and support overrides per-customer.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag tso-service in staging with read-only mode and no enactor calls.
Phase 1: Enable canary mode for internal Redwood workloads (1% traffic) with extended observation window and synthetic load tests.
Phase 2: Gradually open canary to customers with low SLA impact; require PM/owner approval for high-impact families.
Phase 3: Enable auto-apply for low-risk suggestions (confidence > 0.92) and automated canary for medium-risk with automated rollback triggers.
Phase 4: Post-rollout monitoring and retrospective; promote policy defaults to production.
test_plan: Unit tests for deterministic scoring function and policy engine.
Integration tests: simulate suggestion -> tso -> rollout-controller -> canary -> metrics check -> auto-revert path.
Chaos tests: inject tail-latency spikes and ensure rollback is triggered and KV cache cleared cleanly.
E2E demos with a staging customer tenant and synthetic workloads to validate metrics-based gates.
Load test tso-service at expected throughput for Optimize suggestion rate (qps ~= 5k).
metrics: False-positive auto-applies (suggestions auto-applied that later required rollback)
Cost delta realized vs predicted (per suggestion)
Impact on tail latency (P95/P99) for affected routes
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive auto-apply could regress customer SLAs. Mitigation: conservative default policies, require manual approval for high-risk classes.
Risk: Simulation mismatches real traffic. Mitigation: combine simulation with live micro-canary and weight telemetry higher in score.
Risk: Rollback not fast enough under load. Mitigation: precompute rollback plan and ensure atomic KV cache invalidation path is tested and optimized.
Risk: Audit/forensics incomplete for Private installs. Mitigation: provide a local audit sink option and document export format for air-gapped environments.
notes: Security: KMS-based signing for approval ballots; see sec ticket SEC-210
